hinges.side_why: pull bar and cylinder are on the left so the hinges are on the right, and the right jamb is the far side of an angled shot - it is a 4 px line with nothing resolvable on it

extras: three pale inlay strips over the lock-far third of the face
whiteboard and yellow dado tiling in the corridor
notes: Angled shot, skew 0.78 - the leaf projects as a trapezoid 544 px wide at y=400 and 470 px at y=1250, and its bottom edge falls 110 px across 300 px of width, so the bottom-right corner runs off the frame. All x fractions were taken against the LOCAL leaf width at each feature's height. Right side is the camera-near one, so the visible deep reveal is on the LEFT (22 px, tone 0.54) and the right is a 4 px line. The three vertical lines are applied pale strips, not milled grooves: they read 1.5-2x the surrounding face and stop short of both ends, running roughly y 0.06 to 0.92. Everything but the strips and the plaster is dark, so several frame tones come out above 1.0 - they are ratios to a very dark leaf (lum 55), not errors.
